issues.description: Cycle detection in push() may now misfire because 'walking' conflates two prior states
issues.detail: Previously 'working' meant 'children pushed, not yet emitted' and 'walking' meant something else. Collapsing to a single 'walking' state means push() now treats any in-progress node as a potential cycle ancestor. If the prior two-state distinction was load-bearing for distinguishing cycles from already-yielded-but-not-marked-sorted nodes, this could change cycle detection semantics. Worth confirming tests cover this.

issues.description: Moving s.state[k] = sorted inside the !yield-returns-true branch leaves state dirty on early termination
issues.detail: Previously 'sorted' was set unconditionally after the yield check. Now it is only set when yield returns true. If the caller stops iteration via yield returning false, the defer clears state anyway, so this is fine — but if state==sorted nodes are re-encountered in the same loop before return, they will no longer be marked. Verify the stack cannot contain duplicates after yield=false.

issues.description: Typos in updated comment: 'visisted' and 'if its'
issues.detail: The reworded comment introduces 'visisted' (should be 'visited') and 'if its' (should be "if it's"). Minor but worth fixing while touching these lines.

issues.description: clear(s.stack) before reslicing to zero length is redundant for non-pointer element types
issues.detail: clear() on the full-length slice zeroes elements so GC can reclaim referenced Nodes — useful if Node holds pointers. The reslice to [:0] alone would leak references in the backing array, so the clear is intentional. Worth a brief comment explaining the GC rationale to prevent a future 'cleanup' from removing it.

issues.description: No test added demonstrating the state-reuse bug being fixed
issues.detail: PR title says 'Fix state reuse' and 'non-zero elements in the stack slice', but the diff contains no test changes. A regression test invoking Sort twice on the same Sorter with overlapping keys would lock in the fix and prevent future regressions.

review.summary: The PR consolidates two intermediate states into one ('walking'), moves cleanup into a defer, and reorders the sorted-marking to only occur on successful yield. The core fix — deferring clear() so reused Sorter instances start clean — looks correct and addresses a real bug. Main concerns are semantic: collapsing working/walking may affect cycle detection in push(), and moving s.state[k]=sorted inside the yield branch changes when state is recorded. No regression test accompanies the fix despite the PR explicitly being about state reuse. Comment typos are minor.
